items.title: Sebi proposes to expand FPI play in commodities
items.description: In a strategic move, the Securities and Exchange Board of India has unveiled plans to enable foreign investors to trade in commodity derivatives. This initiative is designed to expand engagement within India's commodity derivatives market. International participants will soon be able to trade physically settled non-agricultural contracts, with the requirement to settle positions before the tender period starts.

items.title: Big investors outperform Nifty, bring in double-digit returns
items.description: During Q1 of FY27, marquee investors saw remarkable success, as their stock portfolios delivered returns ranging from 9.7% to a staggering 39.9% between April and June. Ashish Dhawan emerged as the frontrunner, closely followed by other top investors like Ashish Kacholia. Their impressive performance clearly outstripped the Nifty and Nifty 500 market averages, highlighting their substantial stakes in companies with holdings exceeding one thousand crore.

items.title: Stocks in news: L&T, Tata Motors, HAL, Grasim, NBCC and IRCTC
items.description: The Indian equity markets concluded the trading session on a low note, as escalating crude oil prices weighed heavily on worldwide market sentiment. Notable developments included Larsen & Toubro's announcement of a strategic business transfer for its data center services. Focus will also be on firms like Tata Motors and Hindustan Aeronautics.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Indian equity benchmarks concluded lower on Tuesday, August 11, with Nifty 50 falling below 24,500. Crude oil price rebound and F&O expiry volatility impacted investor sentiment significantly. Market momentum now shifts towards the upcoming U.S. Consumer Price Index data release. Foreign portfolio investors net bought shares worth Rs 258.55 crore on Tuesday. The Indian rupee traded weaker, declining around 15 paise to 95.43.

items.title: These 6 banking stocks have an upside potential of up to 25% in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: This is worth noting: Despite sustained periods of FPI selling, banking stocks have not corrected to the extent one might have expected, especially based on what happened four or five years ago. Yes, some stocks have corrected from their 2024 or 2025 highs, but the overall performance has been relatively resilient.Check out Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, for price targets of over 4,000 listed stocks along with detailed company analysis focusing on five key components ,earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum, to generate standardized scores. SR+ Reports is a complimentary offering to ETPrime members.

items.title: Manappuram ends family-led era as Bain brings in a professional MD
items.description: Manappuram Finance will shift to professional management after Bain Capital gained joint control, with VP Nandakumar becoming non-executive chairman and Ashish Singh taking over as MD and CEO from January 2027. First-quarter profit jumped over four-fold to ₹585 crore.

items.title: Stocks to buy in 2026 for long term: Gland Pharma, Star Cement among 5 stocks that could give 10-30% return
items.description: Brokerages remain bullish on a host of stocks, with Star Cement, Poonawalla Fincorp, Hexaware Technologies and Godrej Consumer Products receiving Buy ratings.We have collated a list of recommendations from top brokerage firms from ETNow and other sources:

items.title: Buy, Sell or Hold: Citi recommends buy on Godrej Consumer Products; Goldman Sachs maintains buy on Astra Microwave
items.description: Brokerages remain bullish on Astra Microwave, Kalpataru Projects International and Godrej Consumer Products, citing strong growth prospects, improving financials and stable business strategies. Goldman Sachs raised Astra Microwave’s target on robust margins and order inflows, while Nuvama upgraded Kalpataru Projects after a strong Q1FY27 and better balance sheet.

items.title: MCX shares rise 2% as JPMorgan upgrades, raises target price after this Sebi proposal
items.description: Shares of Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) rose more than 2% after Sebi proposed widening foreign portfolio investors’ access to physically settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives. JPMorgan upgraded MCX to ‘Overweight ’, and Jefferies retained a ‘Buy’ rating, citing the potential for higher trading volumes and earnings.

items.title: Lenskart, Delhivery, among 10 stocks with highest increase in DII holdings in Q1. See full list
items.description: Domestic institutional investors stepped up buying in several stocks during the June quarter, with DII holdings rising sharply across a number of companies. The increase in ownership came alongside varied stock price performances, highlighting the stocks where domestic institutions raised their exposure the most during the quarter. Here’s the full list.

items.title: Senco Gold shares fall over 8% after Q1 results. What squeezed profitability?
items.description: Senco Gold shares fell 8.16% after the company reported mixed Q1 FY27 results. While consolidated revenue surged 67% YoY to Rs 3,056 crore, PAT declined 3% to Rs 101 crore. EBITDA rose 16% to Rs 213 crore, but margins contracted sharply amid promotional discounting, lower gold prices and customs duty changes, weighing on profitability and investor sentiment.

items.title: 44 bullish & bearish stock picks across sectors for August by Axis Direct
items.description: A sector-wise technical outlook points to a broadly positive market trend, with banking, capital goods, realty, consumer durables, healthcare, power and auto sectors showing bullish setups. The brokerage recommends a buy-on-dips strategy across several sectors, while selective caution is advised in FMCG, metals and oil & gas despite their broader technical resilience.

items.title: Manappuram Finance shares jump 3% after Q1 profit soars 4x. Why Jefferies, Morgan Stanley raised target prices
items.description: Manappuram Finance shares witnessed an uptick on Wednesday after Q1 FY27 profit surged nearly four-fold to Rs 585 crore. Jefferies raised its target price to Rs 430, citing better NII and lower provisions, while Morgan Stanley also raised its target. CLSA retained a Hold rating, with a Rs 350 target price.

items.title: FMCG’s FII nightmare! $5.2 billion selloff in 12 straight months. Are stocks set for a rebound?
items.description: Over the past year, foreign investors have unloaded $5.2 billion worth of FMCG stocks, largely due to the challenges stemming from inflated valuations and rising input costs. Companies are now transferring these increased costs to customers, resulting in weak volume growth and declining margins. For a recovery to take shape, analysts emphasize the need for enhanced consumer spending and stable commodity prices.

items.title: Zydus Lifesciences shares drop 3% after Q1 earnings. Here's why Nuvama upgraded rating, hiked target
items.description: Shares of Zydus Lifesciences saw a decline of more than two percent following the announcement of a notable profit drop. The net profit plunged thirty-six percent year-on-year for the first quarter, despite a nearly twenty-two percent increase in operational revenue. Expenses surged by over forty-one percent. However, the managing director remains optimistic about future prospects. Analysts at Nuvama have upgraded the stock to 'Buy', setting a higher price target.

items.title: Missed these IPOs after cold debuts? 11 stocks have since soared up to 222% in few months
items.description: Despite underwhelming debuts for eleven IPOs, the market has witnessed a remarkable recovery in their valuations. Stocks have soared impressively, with gains ranging from 23% to a staggering 222% over their initial offer prices. Notably, Omnitech Engineering rebounded dramatically, rising by 222% after an initial drop of 9.63%. This underscores the fact that performance on listing day may not accurately predict long-term success.

items.title: Sensex falls over 200 points, Nifty below 24,450 as oil nears $90/barrel. What lies ahead?
items.description: On Wednesday, Indian stocks experienced a downturn as oil prices approached $90 per barrel.  Analysts attribute this decline to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, which are hampering market momentum. Despite this, the resilience of India's growth suggests improved corporate earnings for FY27, while mid and small-cap stocks have been highly active due to recent results.

items.title: Godrej Consumer Products shares tank 10% after CEO’s sudden exit; HSBC downgrades to Hold
items.description: Godrej Consumer Products shares declined 10% following the sudden resignation of CEO Sudhir Sitapati, who announced his work was finished and it was time for new beginnings. HSBC nalysts have since downgraded the stock, highlighting potential uncertainties and execution hurdles ahead, despite the company showcasing strong Q1 performance with impressive profit and revenue growth. Aasif Malbari is set to take charge as the new CEO.

items.title: SpaceX namesake creates confusion on Dalal Street! Indian IT stock skyrockets 23% in 2 days
items.description: Blue Cloud Softech Solutions shares surged 23% in two days after its US subsidiary announced a $150 million deal with Malaysia-based SpaceX International. However, the company clarified that the entity has no connection with Elon Musk’s SpaceX. The sharp rally appears to have been driven partly by confusion over the names.

items.title: ideaForge Technology shares drop over 9% in two days. JM Financial downgrades rating
items.description: ideaForge Technology shares fell 9.5% over two days after JM Financial downgraded the stock to Add from Buy, citing valuation concerns following a sharp run-up despite strong long-term prospects. The brokerage expects order inflows to remain weak in FY27 before recovering in FY28 and FY29, while execution momentum and operating leverage could support significant revenue and margin growth.

items.title: TD Power Systems shares rally over 12% after Q1 profit jumps 72% YoY to Rs 86 crore
items.description: TD Power Systems shares surged after the company reported a strong Q1FY27 performance. Profit after tax rose 72% YoY to Rs 86 crore, while revenue and EBITDA jumped 71% and 72%, respectively, driven by robust operational growth.

items.title: Finolex Cables shares jump 10% on strong Q1 performance; revenue crosses Rs 2,000 crore mark
items.description: Finolex Cables shares rose sharply on Wednesday after the company reported a 52.6% YoY rise in Q1 FY27 net profit to Rs 208.2 crore. Revenue surged 44.3% to Rs 2,013.15 crore, crossing the Rs 2,000-crore mark, while EBITDA rose 79% and margins expanded amid strong operational performance.

items.title: TCS, other Tata stocks fall up to 4% as N Chandrasekaran resigns
items.description: Shares of Tata Group companies fell, primarily driven by TCS. N Chandrasekaran stepped down as Tata Sons chairman ahead of the scheduled AGM on August 18, yet he will continue in his role until February 2027. His exit raises questions about the upcoming board meeting, particularly regarding the influence of Tata Trusts, which holds the majority stake.

items.title: Dr Agarwals Health shares fall 7% after Rs 2,065-crore block deal; Hyperion Investments, Claymore likely sellers
items.description: Dr Agarwals Health Care shares dropped on Wednesday after a Rs 2,065-crore block deal involving 4.07 crore shares. Hyperion Investments and Claymore Investments were likely sellers, according to term sheet details. The block deal came after the company reported a 44.6% YoY rise in Q1 FY27 profit to Rs 55 crore.

items.title: CAS chaos: Retail traders call for boycott, declare 'No Trade Day'
items.description: Retail traders are observing a proposed ‘No Trade Day’ on August 12 to protest the newly introduced Closing Auction Session (CAS), higher securities transaction tax and changing market rules. The campaign follows concerns over increased volatility and divergence in closing prices since CAS was introduced.

items.title: Sebi sees no manipulation in new CAS despite participation concerns
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has confirmed that no manipulation exists within the newly established closing auction system. This session, which establishes closing stock prices, strives to meet international norms. Since its inception, participation in the closing auction has progressively increased. The regulator is actively considering feedback to amplify market participation. This reform is essential in reducing tracking discrepancies for passive investment funds.

items.title: Market Trading Guide: 4 stock picks with strong technical setups for this week
items.description: The market outlook remains constructive, with four stocks showing promising technical setups backed by breakouts, improving momentum and supportive moving-average structures. Technical analysis of the following stocks by analysts Himanshu Gupta, Jainam and Nagaraj Shetti of HDFC Securities shows that the stocks are positioned for further upside, with defined support levels and attractive near-term targets offering favourable risk-reward opportunities.Here are 4 stock recommendations:

items.title: NALCO, Hindalco gain up to 8% as global aluminium prices hit 7-week high amid Mideast tensions
items.description: NALCO and Hindalco shares rallied sharply on Wednesday as global aluminium prices hit a seven-week high amid Middle East tensions and fresh supply concerns. A production cut at Brazil’s Alunorte refinery, multi-decade-low LME inventories and disrupted Middle East shipments have tightened the market, supporting aluminium prices and Indian producers.

items.title: Chandrasekaran steps down as chairman of Tata Sons ahead of AGM on August 18
items.description: N Chandrasekaran has stepped down as Tata Sons chairman, ending a significant tenure. ET had first reported Chandrasekaran is considering stepping down as Tata Sons chairman. His departure follows disagreements within Tata Trusts regarding business performance and capital needs. The group's revenue and profit saw substantial growth under his leadership. Chandrasekaran's exit creates a leadership transition for the conglomerate. This occurs as the group makes major investments in new ventures.

items.title: N Chandrasekaran era delivered 3.3X market cap growth. Can Tata stocks keep winning after his exit?
items.description: Tata Group’s combined market value has grown 3.3-fold to Rs 22.5 lakh crore since N Chandrasekaran took charge in 2017. With his exit set for February, investors now face a key question: can Tata stocks sustain their strong wealth creation amid leadership uncertainty and growing company-specific challenges?

items.title: Ashish Kacholia, Vijay Kedia beat Nifty in Q1, portfolios swell up to 40%
items.description: India’s superstar investors outperformed the Nifty in Q1 FY27, with portfolio values rising as much as 40%. Ashish Dhawan led the pack with a nearly 40% gain, followed by Ashish Kacholia and Hemendra Kothari. Vijay Kedia, Akash Bhansali and other marquee investors also posted strong gains, even as the broader market remained cautious amid heightened volatility.

items.title: Ardee Industries shares slip 7% post-listing after double-digit listing gains. What should investors do?
items.description: Ardee Industries shares fell nearly 7% from their BSE listing price after a strong debut, but remained over 29% above the IPO price. With analysts advising IPO allottees to hold with a stop-loss and fresh buyers to wait for dips, here’s what investors should know about the stock.

items.title: Why is market falling today? N Chandra’s exit among 3 factors behind 550-pt Sensex slide; Nifty below 24,300
items.description: The Indian stock market witnessed sharp selling on Wednesday, with the Sensex dropping over 570 points and Nifty sliding below 24,300. The decline was triggered by Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran's resignation and rising crude oil prices, dragging down major Tata Group stocks and erasing over Rs 2 lakh crore in investor wealth.

items.title: Dish TV Q1 loss more than triples to Rs 286 crore; VZY sales cross Rs 200 crore
items.description: Dish TV India reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 286 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, as subscription revenue fell 41% to Rs 161 crore. Total expenses rose 46% amid shifting consumer viewing habits, while the company continued expanding its VZY Smart TV ecosystem to drive connected entertainment.

items.title: Miss just 5 best days of Nifty and lose big: How 21-year data from 2005-2026 shows cost of timing the market
items.description: A 21-year analysis by Abakkus Mutual Fund shows how missing the stock market’s strongest days can significantly hurt long-term returns. For the Nifty 50 TRI, CAGR fell from 13.67% to 11.31% when the best five days were missed, and dropped to just 1% for investors who missed the best 50 days.

items.title: Business is one thing. Stock price is another. 4 small-caps from different sectors with upside potential of up to 33%
items.description: The Nifty and the Sensex are correcting after a few days of gains. While it may seem like the whole market is turning down, remember that the big indices have little to do with the small-cap space. These stocks live in a world of their own. They have had a poor run for more than two years now. And if history is any guide, that kind of phase does not go on forever. The question is how to look at them at a time like this.

items.title: Rupee nudges up on RBI intervention; investors eye inflation data
items.description: The Indian rupee finished the day marginally higher, propelled by ongoing tensions in the Middle East. Continuous interventions from the central bank have provided support against the U.S. dollar. Traders remain watchful as critical inflation data from India and the U.S. approaches. Throughout August, the central bank has actively engaged in the foreign exchange market. Attention is now on forthcoming inflation reports that could influence future monetary policy decisions.

items.title: Marksans Pharma shares rally over 9% after Q1 profit spikes 174% YoY to Rs 159 crore
items.description: Marksans Pharma shares surged after Q1FY27 profit jumped 174% YoY to Rs 159 crore. Revenue rose 35.6% to Rs 841 crore, while EBITDA hit a record Rs 213 crore, driven by strong growth in its UK and Europe formulation businesses.

items.title: Cupid shares jump nearly 9% in two days post Q1 earnings
items.description: Cupid shares gained 8.8% in two days after the company reported a threefold rise in Q1 FY27 net profit to Rs 44 crore, while revenue surged 159% YoY to Rs 155 crore. Strong operating performance, margin expansion and a higher FY27 guidance have strengthened the outlook for the stock.

items.title: Embassy Office Parks REIT to enter Nifty 500, become only investment trust in Nifty Midcap 150
items.description: Embassy Office Parks REIT will be included in the Nifty 500 and Nifty Midcap 150 from September 30, 2026, as part of NSE Indices’ latest periodic review. The REIT will also enter several other broad-based indices, potentially increasing its visibility and participation from institutional and passive investors.

items.title: TCS shares tumble 4%, wipe out Rs 35,000 crore after N Chandrasekaran resigns. What should investors do?
items.description: TCS shares fell nearly 4% after N Chandrasekaran resigned as Tata Sons chairman, wiping ₹35,000 crore from its market value. Analysts called the reaction knee-jerk, while technical indicators point to support near ₹2,000–2,300 and resistance at ₹2,670–2,700.

items.title: Groww shares climb 2% after July client additions; market share rises to 28.88%
items.description: Groww shares rose 1.91% after the company added 70,119 clients in July, taking its active client base to 13.12 million and market share to 28.88%. The stock has gained nearly 27% in 2026 so far, outperforming the Sensex, while remaining 13% below its 52-week high.
